name: Tradie Ute
summary: The owner's dual-cab Mitsubishi Triton (MQ) as a roster car (R123), rebuilt against the owner's photos after the 2026-10-11 review (br-bwju.8): the black flat-top canopy on a flat tray with checker-plate under-tray boxes, the platform roof rack with a wind deflector and a rolled awning on the left, the chrome "dynamic shield" grille with swept headlights on a tall blunt nose, a solid black bull bar (light bar, fog lamps, winch hook), the snorkel on the driver's A-pillar, a small lift, black wheels with a silver lip, plain paint. Rear drive, 1900 kg: heavier and torquier than the Cruz, lower top speed. Detail pass (2026-10-17): the canopy's real hardware (the upper doors' T-handles and gas struts, a louvred vent, the drip rail, chrome corner protectors, amber and red reflectors), its rear door with a tinted window, T-handle and third brake light, a seat-coloured lid with tie-down rails, door handles, the chrome shoulder line and the J-line where the cab meets the tray, the black rocker, and taller tray lamps; the paint stays plain, as on the owner's car. Before and after: docs/evidence/br-bwju.8/ute-before-after-views.png.

reference.note: The compare below is LOD0 against the owner's Triton mesh in four views. "The reference sheet itself" opens LOD0's side against the owner's side photo: a hand-traced outline of Screenshot_20240415_085850, IoU 0.717 (docs/evidence/br-bwju.8/reference-photo/score.json; the photo itself stays private: number plate and house). Left to right per view: the reference silhouette, the model's, and the diff (green is model outside the reference, red is reference the model misses), bounding-box normalised. The model is a caricature, wider and lower than the real car, and the photo has perspective, so these IoUs measure a likeness, not a scan. Front and rear three-quarter views are in the turntable.
